# DecisionTools
中文 · Releases · MIT
Optional Decision API assistance for **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**. A small bounded-answer model recomm
ends tools before the main model's first request and can prefetch useful search sources. The main mo
del keeps control; **every tool stays available** through ordinary discovery and existing permission
l keeps control; **every tool stays available** through ordinary discovery and existing permissions.
Requires DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2` and Node `>=22.19.0`. The settings UI currently uses Chinese labels. No
build step or runtime npm dependencies.

ll into a different CLI profile expecting it to appear in Desktop.

The format-1 index pins the installable release to an exact Git commit. This is an author-maintained

## Configure
1. Open **Settings → DecisionTools**. Enter your Decision API URL, credential and authentication mod

e (`bearer`, `api-key`, or `none`).
2. Choose **探测服务与模型** (probe service and models). Probing never

selects a model.
3. Select a discovered model yourself, then **测试所选模型并保存** (test selected model and

save). You can instead save connection details with the model empty and assistance disabled.
4. Enab
le the saved model when wanted. The leading lightning icon on a session's hover toolbar toggles **De

cisionBoost** for that session.
5. Optionally enable **搜索候选预选与正文预读** (search-source selection and pr
efetch), which is off initially.
There is no default service, key, selected model, or automatic activation. D3 ultra receives a recom
mendation label if discovered; it is not selected automatically. Compatible services, including self
-hosted endpoints, can be used instead. Disabling the feature takes effect without restarting DSH.
## How it works
- On the **first request of a new genuine user input**, the decision service scores tool names and s
hort descriptions. Exact definitions for up to six confident recommendations are then fetched **loca

lly** and supplied to the main model. It can use them directly or discover other tools normally.
- A
dvice is not repeatedly injected after that task has entered execution. Agent relays, tool results,

pending unclaimed messages and image-only messages do not become decision tasks.
- Errors, incompati
ble responses, abstention and timeouts leave ordinary discovery intact. Tool selection defaults to a

6-second deadline; repeated failures open a short circuit breaker.
- Optional search assistance ran
ks existing candidates, then invokes the existing reader for up to three relevant pages. The complet
e search result and **all candidates remain unchanged**. Excerpts are at most 6,000 characters each

and are marked untrusted and potentially truncated; ordinary full reading remains available.
- Repea
ted reads can reuse a short-lived result only for the same Agent, task, exact reader arguments and t
ool definition. Original guards and pre/post policies still apply. Session/global changes cancel old
waits and reject stale results.
No tool is unregistered, no execution permission is added, and no main-model configuration, precisio
n or conversation history is changed. This is advisory acceleration, not an autonomous planner or a
replacement for the main model.
### Supported protocols and search tools
Jev/SystemOne-style `state + questions` requests with validated `score`, `noul`, and `choice` answer
s. Common `answers`, `results`, and `data.answers` wrappers are accepted. Model probing tries `/v1/s
ystemone/models`, `/v1/models`, and `/api/info`; custom paths and proxy prefixes can be configured.
Noncompatible Decision APIs are not guaranteed to work.
Search adapters currently cover native `web_search` (`sources`) with `web_fetch`, and `mcp__web__sea
rch` with `mcp__web__fetch_content`. MCP candidates may be structured JSON or the observed `Found N
search results / URL / Summary` format. Unknown formats fall back unchanged; arbitrary MCP servers a
re not automatically supported.
## Data and privacy
When enabled, your selected Decision service receives the current user task plus tool names and shor
t descriptions. Search assistance additionally sends the actual search query and candidate titles, U
RLs and short snippets. It does **not deliberately send** complete schemas, tool execution results,
full fetched pages, file contents or full conversation histories. A task or description can itself c
ontain sensitive data; credential-pattern redaction is best effort, not a data-loss prevention guara
ntee. Enable external services only for data you may share with them.
Credentials are stored using DSH's credentials service, not the ordinary settings JSON or status log
s. Public services require HTTPS; loopback HTTP is permitted; redirects are rejected. Speculative pa
ge prefetch refuses obvious private-address URLs and credential-bearing query parameters; the actual
reader and its existing network policies remain responsible for DNS/redirect/network enforcement.
Local state lives under `$DSH_HOME/decisiontools`, or `~/.dsh/decisiontools`: connection/settings, p
er-session switches and recent status. Status contains session identifiers, task hashes, tool names,
model identifiers, counts and timings, not task or page bodies. Do not upload a user's profile as a
bug report. See SECURITY.md.
